paper text.text:
The paths $apc,brd$ and the edge $cd$ give $B\cup H_0$ as a minor
of $G$, so it has no $K_5$ minor. Every $K_{3,3}$ subdivision in it
uses $cd$, since $B+ac+bd$ is planar. Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms}
with $cd$ required gives $2{,}104$ candidates. Here $B\cup K_4[A]$
is three-connected, $L$ has no $K_5$ minor, and no degree-three
interior vertex is adjacent to both ends of $cd$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:independent-neighborhood}(a). With the planarity
conditions above, the checks in~\supp{E7} leave nine labeled
bridges, giving the five displayed forms up to interchanging $A_1,A_2$.

In case (i) of Lemma~\ref{dis:type-b-forms}, the nine labeled bridges
and the two choices of added edge give $18$ graphs. Sixteen have a
proper nontoroidal minor and the other two are isomorphic to
$\mathfrak T_{66}$~\supp{E7}. Suppose (ii) holds. Replacing $ce,df$
in the nonplanar simple-face test by $cqe,dzf$ gives a connected
nonplanar subgraph $S$ of $G-aq$. In a torus embedding of this proper
minor, every face of $S$ is a disk by Lemma~\ref{lem:torus-complement}.

B + K4[a,b,c,d].meaning: B plus all six edges among a, b, c, d

B + cd.meaning: B + cd, a subgraph of G since P_x = cd

Psi1 + B.meaning: the graph consisting of Psi_1 and B, with P_x = cd and P_w shortened to ef: twins p, q on {a, c, e} and r, z on {b, d, f}, where e = s_w, f = t_w

vertex names: the attachments a = s_m, b = t_m, c = s_x, d = t_x of B; interior vertices of B are u0, u1, ...; for the bridges that pass, the paper's names are given with the verdict

excluded by a hypothesis of the case.fact: an interior vertex of degree three has two adjacent neighbours
excluded by a hypothesis of the case.why it excludes the bridge: Lemma 3.4(a); the edges added in the test graph are edges of G.
Lemma 4.29 shows that B + ac + bd is planar.

excluded by a hypothesis of the case.fact: B plus all edges among a, b, c, d has a cut of at most two vertices
excluded by a hypothesis of the case.why it excludes the bridge: Three-connectivity of B ∪ K_4[{a,b,c,d}], used with Construction 3.18.

verdicts.K5 minor: a K5 minor in the named graph, which is a minor of G
verdicts.proper nontoroidal minor: an allowed reduction of B (Section 3) after which the named test graph is still nonplanar; the proof shows that this gives a proper nontoroidal minor of G
verdicts.isomorphic to a bridge given in the text: B passes every test of the case and is isomorphic to a bridge given in the text (listed under "bridges given in the text"); the record that it passes the tests is kept with the verdict

whole graphs: For each bridge that passes, the two graphs of Lemma 4.29(i): G = (Psi_1 ∪ B) + eb and G = (Psi_1 ∪ B) + af, with P_x = cd and P_w = ef. Proposition 4.30 cites this part for the claim that these give only T66. The exterior formed by a bridge uv on {c,d,e,f} is treated in the paper by argument, so it is not included here.
